A Reform UK councillor has complained to Parliament about MP Sam Carling over a 199-home development between Ramsey and Bury. Cllr Karan Maheshwari, who represents Ramsey on Huntingdonshire District Council, has submitted a complaint to the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards. It concerns North West Cambridgeshire MP Mr Carling’s response to Cllr Maheshwari’s request for him to intervene in planning application 25/01382/OUT, for 199 homes between Ramsey and Bury. A copy seen by this publication is dated November 2 and marked “DRAFT – NOT SUBMITTED”, but Cllr Maheshwari later confirmed he submitted it on November 3 and received confirmation on November 4. The dispute began after Huntingdonshire District Council’s development management committee said it was minded to reject the scheme. Cllr Maheshwari says he asked Mr Carling to urge the Secretary of State not to “call in” the application. A planning application being called in means the Government takes responsibility for deciding it instead of leaving the final decision with the local authority. rawItems.content: A five-bedroom property in Godmanchester is up for sale at offers over £850,000. The link-detached house on Old Court Hall has been completely refurbished by the current owners. rawItems.title: Here is some of Huntingdonshire's most unusual bridges and where to find them
rawItems.content: From a medieval bridge with its own chapel to a 55-arch causeway, Huntingdonshire is packed with unusual crossings. The district’s rivers, floodplains and Fenland waterways have shaped travel for centuries, leaving medieval crossings and Fen drainage bridges behind. Here are some of Huntingdonshire’s most striking bridges and where to find them. St Ives Bridge One of the county’s most extraordinary bridges spans the River Great Ouse at St Ives. The town’s first bridge was built of wood in 1107, before work began on a stone replacement in the early 15th century. The stone crossing was completed in 1425, and a chapel was added the following year. It is one of only three bridges in England with a chapel. The bridge also still bears the scars of the English Civil War. Parliamentary troops destroyed part of it to hinder Royalist forces, so a temporary drawbridge was installed. When the damaged section was rebuilt in 1716, it was given rounded arches instead of matching the pointed medieval ones, leaving a visible difference today. The chapel has also served as a toll house, inn and private home. The bridge is also a scheduled monument. items.title: Great Whyte Pedestrian Safety & Speed Limit Review
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Minutes (Agenda - Full Council 12 November 2026): Council resolved to submit a formal request to Cambridgeshire County Council Highways for a 20mph speed zone and upgraded zebra crossing along Great Whyte, following resident traffic survey feedback.

items.title: Planning Committee Recommends Refusal for 25 Dwellings Off Oilmills Road
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Planning Meeting agenda 20261022): Unanimously recommended refusal for outline application 26/00142/OUT on grounds of highway safety on Oilmills Road, surface water flood risk, and overdevelopment beyond the settlement boundary.

items.title: Planning Committee Approves High Street Commercial Refurbishment & Signage
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Planning Minutes (Planning Meeting agenda 20261022): Supported planning application 26/00188/FUL for commercial shopfront renovation and heritage signage in the Ramsey Conservation Area.
